shortDescription: Enterprise workspace messaging platform with granular bot and user OAuth 2.0 scopes.
overview: Slack enables AI agents to read channel messages, post automated notifications, respond in threads, and interact with team members. Slack uses an OAuth 2.0 v2 authorization code flow with distinct token types: bot tokens (`xoxb-`) for autonomous agent actions and user tokens (`xoxp-`) for acting on behalf of a specific user.
intendedUseCase: Connecting an AI agent to send channel alerts, summarize conversations, create triage tickets from mentions, or execute commands inside Slack.

difficultyExplanation.overallSummary: Creating a custom Slack app and installing it in your own workspace is fast (15-20 min) and requires 0 external wait time. Complexity arises from navigating bot vs user scopes, the strict prohibition of mixing SIWS (Sign in with Slack) scopes with bot scopes, and workspace admin approval policies.

steps.title: Create App in Slack Developer Portal
steps.whatToDo: Navigate to api.slack.com/apps, click 'Create New App', and select 'From scratch'. Provide an App Name and select your development workspace.
steps.whyItMatters: Initializes the app entity and allocates a unique Client ID, Client Secret, and Signing Secret.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: You are redirected to the 'Basic Information' page displaying App Credentials (Client ID and App ID).
steps.failureRemedies: Ensure you are signed in with the correct Slack workspace account. If workspace is restricted, request App Creation permissions from workspace admin.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires logging into your Slack account and associating the app with your organization's workspace.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Redirect URLs
steps.whatToDo: In the left sidebar under 'Features', click 'OAuth & Permissions'. Scroll to 'Redirect URLs', click 'Add New Redirect URL', enter your HTTPS callback URI, and click 'Save URLs'.
steps.whyItMatters: Slack strictly validates incoming authorization requests against this exact URL list. Mismatched or non-HTTPS URLs cause 'bad_redirect_uri' errors.
informationNeeded: Valid HTTPS callback URL (or http://localhost for local dev)
steps.howToVerifyComplete: The redirect URL appears in the saved list with a green confirmation toast.
steps.failureRemedies: Check that the URL has no anchor tag (#). Verify protocol is HTTPS unless using localhost. Ensure multiple redirect URIs are explicitly entered.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent can validate URL formatting, ensure absence of anchors, and check TLS status; developer pastes into Slack UI.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Validate callback URL syntax, port constraints, and TLS certificate readiness.

steps.title: Add Bot and User Permission Scopes
steps.whatToDo: On the 'OAuth & Permissions' page, scroll down to 'Scopes'. Under 'Bot Token Scopes', add minimal necessary permissions such as `chat:write`, `channels:read`, and `channels:history`. Do NOT add Sign in with Slack scopes here.
steps.whyItMatters: Slack's v2 OAuth enforces least-privilege. Adding excess scopes increases installation friction and admin rejections.
informationNeeded: List of required API methods for agent features
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Selected scopes appear in the Bot Token Scopes table.
steps.failureRemedies: If a scope conflict occurs, verify you haven't mixed `openid`/`email` SIWS scopes with `chat:write` bot scopes.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent analyzes required agent capabilities and generates the exact least-privilege scope list.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Verify scope list against Slack method documentation and check for known scope conflict pairs.

steps.title: Install App to Workspace for Testing
steps.whatToDo: Scroll to top of 'OAuth & Permissions' and click 'Install to Workspace' (or 'Reinstall to Workspace' if scopes changed). Review the consent permissions and click 'Allow'.
steps.whyItMatters: Issues an initial Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-...`) for immediate local testing and verifies the consent screen behavior.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: A Bot User OAuth Token starting with `xoxb-` is displayed on the page.
steps.failureRemedies: If button says 'Request to Install', submit the request to your workspace admin or test in a personal developer sandbox workspace.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires granting OAuth permissions to your workspace data.

steps.title: Implement OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Exchange
steps.whatToDo: Build authorization link: `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&redirect_uri=...`. On callback, exchange `code` via POST to `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access` with `client_id` and `client_secret`.
steps.whyItMatters: Enables multi-user or multi-tenant installations so any authorized user can link their Slack workspace to your agent.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Response returns `{ ok: true, access_token: 'xoxb-...', team: { id: '...', name: '...' } }`.
steps.failureRemedies: If `bad_redirect_uri` occurs, confirm `redirect_uri` sent to `/oauth.v2.access` exactly matches the one in the initial authorization link.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent can write, format, and test the backend code for authorization URL generation and token exchange.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Perform automated mock exchange and schema validation on response payload.

overview: Notion provides two primary integration models: Internal Connections (using static API tokens for your own workspace) and Public Connections (using OAuth 2.0 for multi-tenant agent apps). steps.title: Decide Connection Type: Internal vs Public
steps.whatToDo: Evaluate your agent's distribution: If your agent will only access your personal or company workspace, create an 'Internal Connection' (which gives an instant API token with no OAuth flow). If users outside your organization will connect, create a 'Public Connection'.
steps.whyItMatters: Internal connections require zero OAuth code, saving hours of development for internal tools. Public connections require full OAuth 2.0 exchange.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Selected 'Public' or 'Internal' during initial integration creation.
steps.failureRemedies: You can convert an internal connection to public later under the connection settings.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires strategic architectural decision on product distribution.

steps.title: Create Public Connection in Notion Developer Portal
steps.whatToDo: Navigate to notion.so/profile/integrations, click 'New connection', choose 'Public', enter App Name, upload logo, and select the associated Notion workspace.
steps.whyItMatters: Registers your OAuth client and generates your Client ID, Client Secret, and authorization endpoint URL.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Connection is created and configuration tabs ('Configuration', 'Distribution') become visible.
steps.failureRemedies: Verify you are logged in as a Notion user with verified email.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires logging into Notion and submitting connection profile data.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs and Distribution
steps.whatToDo: In connection settings, open the 'Configuration' tab. Under 'OAuth Domain & URIs', enter your HTTPS Redirect URI (e.g. `https://myapp.com/api/auth/notion/callback`). Set 'Installation Scope' to either 'Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces'.
steps.whyItMatters: Notion redirects users to this exact URI with an authorization code. If not configured, authorization fails immediately.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Redirect URI is saved and appears in the list.
steps.failureRemedies: Ensure the URL uses HTTPS (except localhost for testing) and has no trailing query parameters.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent verifies callback URL format and HTTPS compliance; developer enters it into Notion dashboard.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Validate callback URL syntax and HTTPS readiness.

steps.title: Build the Authorization URL
steps.whatToDo: Construct the authorization link: `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?client_id={CLIENT_ID}&response_type=code&owner=user&redirect_uri={REDIRECT_URI}&state={STATE}`. Notice `owner=user` is required by Notion.
steps.whyItMatters: Directs prospective users to Notion's consent and page-picker dialog.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Visiting the URL displays the Notion connection prompt asking user to select pages to share.
steps.failureRemedies: If page shows invalid client, confirm the client_id string is exact and integration status is active.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent generates the compliant URL format with required Notion query parameters.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Validate query parameters against Notion OAuth specification.

steps.title: Exchange Code for Access Token via HTTP Basic Auth
steps.whatToDo: On receiving the `code` at your callback, make a POST to `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token` with header `Authorization: Basic {base64(client_id:client_secret)}` and body `{ grant_type: 'authorization_code', code, redirect_uri }`. Also include header `Notion-Version: 2022-06-28`.
steps.whyItMatters: Unlike providers that accept credentials in the POST body, Notion strictly requires HTTP Basic Auth header encoding for client credentials.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Returns `{ access_token: 'ntn_...', workspace_id: '...', workspace_name: '...', bot_id: '...' }`.
steps.failureRemedies: If HTTP 401 Unauthorized occurs, check that `client_id:client_secret` is base64 encoded and properly placed in `Authorization: Basic ...` header.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent can write the exact backend token exchange function and header construction.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Verify basic auth header generation and body payload structure.

difficultyExplanation.overallSummary: Google Drive is one of the most rigorously audited OAuth providers. While creating a project in Google Cloud Console takes 20-30 minutes, production verification requires domain ownership in Google Search Console, YouTube demo video submission, 3-7 business days of manual Google Trust & Safety review for sensitive scopes, and up to $15,000 + 4-8 weeks for Restricted scope CASA audits if requesting broad Drive access.

steps.title: Create Project and Enable Google Drive API
steps.whatToDo: In Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com), create a new project or select an existing one. Navigate to 'APIs & Services' > 'Library', search for 'Google Drive API', and click 'Enable'.
steps.whyItMatters: Enables Drive API endpoints and activates quota allocation for your GCP project.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: API Library displays 'API Enabled' with options to manage metrics and quotas.
steps.failureRemedies: Ensure you have billing enabled on the GCP account if required by your organization tier.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires logging into Google Cloud Console and managing project resources.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
steps.whatToDo: Go to 'APIs & Services' > 'OAuth consent screen'. Select User Type ('Internal' if Google Workspace org only, or 'External' for public users). Fill in App Name, User Support Email, Developer Contact Info, and App Domain URLs (Homepage, Privacy Policy, Terms).
steps.whyItMatters: Defines the branding, policies, and trust information presented to users when connecting Drive.

steps.howToVerifyComplete: Consent screen summary is saved in 'Testing' mode.
steps.failureRemedies: Authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console before they can be added to External apps.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires legally binding developer disclosures and domain verification.

steps.title: Select Scopes: Choose Sensitive (`drive.file`) over Restricted (`drive`)
steps.whatToDo: In Step 2 of the consent screen wizard, click 'Add or Remove Scopes'. Filter for Drive API. Select `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` (Sensitive: per-file access). Avoid `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` (Restricted: full Drive access) unless strictly necessary.
steps.whyItMatters: Crucial product architecture decision: `drive.file` qualifies for sensitive scope verification (3-5 days, no fee), whereas `drive` requires a mandatory third-party CASA Tier 2/Tier 3 audit costing $1,500-$15,000 annually.
informationNeeded: Scope requirement analysis for agent use case
steps.howToVerifyComplete: `drive.file` is listed under 'Sensitive scopes' table.
steps.failureRemedies: If full drive access is unavoidable, prepare budget and architecture documentation for the Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA).
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent audits agent tool calls to minimize scope footprint and prevent accidental restricted scope classification.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Validate proposed scopes against Google CASA tier classifications.

steps.title: Add Test Users (Bypasses Verification for Dev)
steps.whatToDo: In Step 3 of the wizard ('Test users'), click 'Add Users' and enter the email addresses of developers and testers who will authenticate the app during development (up to 100 users).
steps.whyItMatters: Allows immediate end-to-end OAuth testing while the app is still unverified. Without this, external users receive an `access_denied` error (Error 403: org_internal or app_in_testing).
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Emails appear in the Test Users table.
steps.failureRemedies: Make sure emails are valid Google or Google Workspace accounts.
steps.responsibilityReason: Requires managing sensitive internal tester email addresses.

steps.title: Create OAuth 2.0 Web Client Credentials
steps.whatToDo: Navigate to 'APIs & Services' > 'Credentials' > 'Create Credentials' > 'OAuth client ID'. Select Application Type: 'Web application'. Enter 'Authorized JavaScript origins' and 'Authorized redirect URIs' (e.g. `https://myapp.com/api/auth/google/callback`). Click 'Create'.
steps.whyItMatters: Generates the official `client_id` and `client_secret` used by your agent's backend.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: A modal displays your Client ID and Client Secret, and downloads a JSON credentials file.
steps.failureRemedies: Google does not permit wildcards or path fragments in redirect URIs. IP addresses are blocked (use localhost for local dev).
steps.responsibilityReason: Secret credential generation and download.

steps.title: Implement Token Exchange with Offline Access
steps.whatToDo: Build authorization URL with parameters: `response_type=code`, `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`. On callback, exchange code at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` via POST. Store both `access_token` and `refresh_token`.
steps.whyItMatters: `access_type=offline` and `prompt=consent` are mandatory to receive a `refresh_token`. Google access tokens expire after 1 hour (3600 seconds).
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Response contains `access_token`, `expires_in: 3599`, `token_type: 'Bearer'`, and `refresh_token`.
steps.failureRemedies: If no refresh_token is returned, verify `prompt=consent` is included in the initial authorization link.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent writes backend code with proper offline access parameters and token refresh logic.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Verify authorization query parameters include access_type=offline and prompt=consent.

steps.title: Configure Domain-Based Redirect URIs
steps.whatToDo: Under the 'Auth' tab, scroll to 'Redirect URL'. Add your HTTPS callback endpoint (e.g. `https://myapp.com/api/auth/hubspot/callback`). Note: HubSpot does NOT permit IP addresses.
steps.whyItMatters: HubSpot validates the redirect URL during both authorization and token exchange. Discrepancies cause `invalid_request` or `bad_client`.

steps.failureRemedies: Use a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). IP addresses like `http://192.168.1.1` are rejected by HubSpot validation.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent verifies domain structure, HTTPS protocol, and rejects IP addresses.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Validate callback URL does not use IP addresses and uses HTTPS.

steps.title: Select Granular Scopes and Optional Scopes
steps.whatToDo: Under 'Scopes', select required scopes (e.g. `crm.objects.contacts.read`, `crm.objects.deals.read`). Use the `optional_scope` parameter for features tied to higher HubSpot tiers (e.g. Enterprise Custom Objects).
steps.whyItMatters: If a user on a free HubSpot tier tries to install an app with an un-owned tier scope, authorization fails. Using `optional_scope` allows graceful fallback.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Scopes appear checked under App Auth settings.
steps.failureRemedies: Separate mandatory basic scopes from tier-specific features.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent identifies least-privilege CRM scopes and configures optional_scope parameters.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Verify scope list against HubSpot v3 CRM API taxonomy.

steps.title: Implement Token Exchange & 30-Minute Refresh Routine
steps.whatToDo: Build authorization URL: `https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=...&redirect_uri=...`. On callback, POST to `https://api.hubapi.com/oauth/v3/token` with `grant_type=authorization_code`. Schedule refresh token execution prior to the 1800-second expiration.
steps.whyItMatters: HubSpot access tokens expire in 30 minutes. If tokens are not proactively refreshed with the `refresh_token`, subsequent API calls fail with 401 Unauthorized.
steps.howToVerifyComplete: Response contains `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and `expires_in: 1800`.
steps.failureRemedies: Ensure request content-type is `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and credentials are in request body.
steps.responsibilityReason: Agent writes token exchange, storage, and automated proactive token refresh scheduling code.
steps.safeCheckDescription: Verify POST request structure against HubSpot v3 token endpoint schema.
